$comment: Role -> (coding agent x model) mapping for contributed capacity.
This EXTENDS the model already in lib/matrix-agent.js rather than replacing it. That file
defines the six roles, the three tiers, each role's default tier, and tier subsumption
(strong superset-of medium superset-of lightweight). All of that is preserved verbatim here.
What it does NOT define is which non-Claude runtimes qualify: TIER_RUNTIME maps a tier to a
single { runtime: 'claude', model } pair. A contributor lending Octos on Kimi K3, or Codex,
has nothing to match against. `tiers[].accepts` is that missing enumeration.
Why an enumeration and not a score: what a provider exposes upward to HAgency is a ROLE, so
the project side must be able to trust that 'System Architect' means something. A free-form
capability string would make the role name unfalsifiable.

verified: roles, tiers, defaultTier and subsumption: lib/matrix-agent.js:11-35
claude model ids: the Claude 5 family (opus-5, sonnet-5, haiku-4-5, fable-5)
gpt-5.6-sol: observed in the codex CLI's own session banner, codex-cli 0.146.0
framework ids and their model/provider flags: lib/frameworks/*.json
provider + model + reasoning are real fields: backend-v2.js:713 normalizeRuntimeProfileRole
unverified: Octos and Hermes model strings below are the provider FAMILIES the operator named, not
strings read off an installed CLI. Confirm each against `octos --help` / the provider's
own config before relying on an exact match; the family is what the tier turns on.

architect.note: Cross-cutting design. The tier floor is the point: a lightweight model produces plausible architecture that does not survive contact with the codebase.

review.note: lib/matrix-agent.js:26 — 'Cross-model review = staff review from two different model families at strong.' A reviewer SHOULD come from a different family than the author, so this role is the one where a provider offering only one family cannot fill both sides alone.

$acceptsComment: A combination qualifies for a role if its tier rank is >= the role's defaultTier rank.
Subsumption is inherited from matrix-agent.js, so `strong` entries also fill `medium` and
`lightweight` roles — a contributor lending only Opus can serve every role, and pays Opus
rates to write documentation. That trade-off belongs to the contributor, so the console
shows it rather than preventing it.
$excludedComment: Stated rather than implied. A role card that simply omits Haiku reads as an oversight;
one that names the exclusion is a decision the contributor can argue with.
$budgetComment: Per-agent capacity budget: the ceiling is attached to the AGENT, whose model is fixed by
its runtimeProfile — e.g. one Claude Code agent on Opus, 5,000,000 tokens per month.
Consequence the console must show: an engagement draws on one agent's ceiling, so two
projects wanting an architect served by the same Opus agent SHARE that 5M. Over-commitment
is therefore per agent, not against a global pool.
NEITHER FIELD IS ENFORCED TODAY. There is no token accounting anywhere in this repo — every
`usage`/`budget` match in lib/ and backend-v2.js is a CLI help string. Until that exists a
ceiling is a declaration of intent, and the console must label it as one.
